priority.summary: Fermi Inc. discloses the immediate resignation of director Miles Everson, effective July 10, 2026, due to a disagreement over access to company books and records and the delegation of responsibility for overseeing financing transactions to the Finance Committee. Everson's resignation was submitted in a letter, which is attached to the filing as an exhibit, and he did not serve on any committee of the Board at the time of his resignation. The company believes Everson was granted full access to its books and records, except for materials related to pending litigation involving Toby Neugebauer, whom Everson represented on the Board.

Meta Boosts Equity Offering to $98 Billion, Raising Its AI Bet
general.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow takes a look at Meta's plan to boost its equity offering to almost $98 billion, one of the largest ever, as it raises its bet on AI. Plus, Anthropic's IPO could be a defining test for the AI boom, as its S-1 filing reveals staggering growth, spending and losses. And, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey explains why the defense tech firm is teaming up with chipmaker Qualcomm to build a laptop with a US supply chain. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Anduril's Luckey Partners With Qualcomm to Build American-Made Laptop
general.summary: Defense tech startup Anduril is joining forces with chipmaker Qualcomm to build a new American-made laptop, called BlueChip. Anduril founder Palmer Luckey explains why the country's military and critical industries need computers that are fully built domestically and why his company is best placed to do it out of its drone-making plant in Ohio. Luckey speaks with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: South Africa Corn Plantings Seen at Seven-Year Low on El Niño Risk
general.summary: South African commercial corn farmers plan to cut plantings to the smallest area since 2019, squeezed by higher input costs and expectations of a drought during the nation’s summer months.
